definition: A rollback is counted only when it was executed: a merged change reverted, or a schema migration rolled back with the earlier binary started on the rolled-back data, and the result checked by the gate or an installed smoke (a smoke step for a feature the rollback removed is expected to fail, and the entry says so). Each event names its raw evidence; tools/sdlc-metrics.mjs refuses to run if a listed file is missing. Rollback plans, rollback descriptions and engine resumes are not rollbacks. Reverts that landed on main are counted from git separately: commits reachable from main (origin/main when there is no local main) whose subject starts with 'Revert "'; a revert merged into main from a branch has landed on main and counts. Entries under notCounted are kept with the reason they do not meet this definition.

notCounted.what: Pre-run V4 then V3 rollback on a stopped-data copy, then re-applied and smoked
notCounted.reason: The schema was rolled back (V4 then V3, Flyway history and row hashes verified), but the binary then started on it was the current candidate, which re-applied V3 and V4 before the smoke (rollback-verification.md step 4). The earlier binary never ran on the rolled-back schema, so this is a rollback rehearsal of the schema only, not a counted rollback. The final rehearsal on 30f8de4e, which did start the earlier jar, is counted.
